parts.note: reads as a vague phrase about the start of some escalation, but means the literal first block laid ceremonially when a building goes up

explanation.surface: Someone asks what lies at the root of a gradual escalation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Build-up' suggests a growing tension or crowd; read literally it is a building being put up, whose ceremonial first block is the basis.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial block laid at the start of construction is literally the base on which a building rises.

clue.text: Restless excitement when suffering high temperature at headland

parts.note: running a high temperature means being feverish
a ness is a headland or promontory, common in Scottish place names such as Loch Ness

explanation.surface: Someone running a fever on a clifftop feels agitated and keyed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated, restless excitement is described figuratively as a fever pitch of feeling.

explanation.surface: A driver pushed on when someone insisted.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive onwards is to push forward, and to be pressed is to be strongly encouraged or exhorted.

clue.text: Assume angler is at this racecourse

parts.note: to don clothes or an air is to assume them
a caster is one who casts a line, an angler

explanation.surface: A fisherman supposedly turns up at a racing venue.
explanation.walkthrough: DONCASTER is a town in Yorkshire with a famous racecourse, home of the St Leger horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire town hosts a well-known horse-racing track, so the place names the course.

clue.text: The ones over here taking American hero

parts.note: these refers to the ones nearby, over here
US is the abbreviation for American (United States)

explanation.surface: The locals here take on an American champion.
explanation.walkthrough: The hero is the Greek mythological figure who slew the Minotaur.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Athenian king who killed the Minotaur is a classic hero of Greek myth.

clue.text: I rant about in spectacles on the lake

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the two rings of the glasses

parts.note: a pair of glasses looks like two O letters side by side

indicators.note: about signals the letters of I rant are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wearing glasses complains loudly while out on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I RANT to NTARI, and 'in' puts that between the two O's of the spectacles; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America bears this name.

parts.note: a lad is a boy or son

explanation.surface: A boy is put in charge of the audio.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to sound waves or audible noise.

parts.note: reads as a quip about a long nap, but describes sleeping past the intended waking time

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person took rather more than a brief nap.
explanation.walkthrough: Forty winks is a short nap; having more than that suggests sleeping beyond when one meant to wake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeping too long and missing the alarm is exactly napping beyond a brief doze.

parts.note: Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A vegetarian is named after a celestial body.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats no animal products at all certainly avoids meat.

explanation.surface: Something was offered while lasting more time.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out a hand is to stretch it forth, and something lengthened is made longer.

clue.text: Give up telly for a toy

parts.note: to jack in is British slang for to quit or give up
the box is informal British slang for the television

explanation.surface: Someone abandons television in favour of a plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack in' is British slang for quit, and 'the box' and 'telly' are both British informal words for TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's novelty toy where a figure springs out of a case when the lid opens.

indicators.note: in places the turned word for help within the word for class

parts.note: rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

indicators.note: returned indicates the word for help is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Spread the word that assistance has come back to the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads the word for help backwards, and 'in' puts it inside the word for class; 'class' looks like a noun for a group of pupils but means a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread outwards from a centre is to emit or diffuse, like spreading information widely.

parts.note: Rick is a short form of the name Richard

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters of has are shifted into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A man called Richard has taken away a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved, rearranging HAS into SHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled vehicle pulled by a person, a variant spelling of rickshaw, is a passenger carriage.

parts.note: an arrow's long stem and a narrow beam of light share one word, so the phrase describes a ray piercing through

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a word for a bright beam like a dart from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both the long body of an arrow and a narrow beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an arrow's stem and a narrow ray of light breaking through clouds.

indicators.note: from suggests the designer is made out of the letters of the arctic, rearranged

explanation.surface: A building designer comes from the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you the answer is made out of the letters of THE ARCTIC, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who plans and draws up buildings is a designer of structures.

explanation.surface: A doctor does an unplanned check on a child with an itchy rash.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: chickenpox brings out spots, so a check for it is a literal check for spots.
explanation.definitionFit: An unscheduled sample inspection is a random check, and checking a rash is examining marks on the skin.

clue.text: Pass Greek character with Latin plant

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
cum is the Latin word for with

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a pass with a Greek and a Latin speaker to find a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumn crocus or meadow saffron belongs to this flowering genus.

clue.text: Again cur struggled annexing a country!

indicators.note: annexing means attaching the letter a on to the end
struggled suggests the letters of again cur are thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog fights once more while a nation is seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggled' rearranges AGAIN CUR into NICARAGU, and 'annexing' tacks A on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American republic lying between Honduras and Costa Rica.

clue.text: One from southern Europe racing round with hidden energy

indicators.note: with hidden means a letter is tucked inside the rearranged letters
round suggests the letters of racing are spun about into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean athlete laps the track with energy in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges RACING to GRCIAN, and 'with hidden' tucks E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Greece, a country in southern Europe, is described by this term.

clue.text: A question of a mite, say, living in water

indicators.note: say signals that the words for a mite are spoken, giving similar letters

parts.note: a tick is a small blood-sucking arachnid of the mite group

explanation.surface: A question about whether a tiny bug lives underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you A TICK is spoken, giving ATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Creatures dwelling in water, such as fish, are described with this adjective.

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of out are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A northern town was left out of the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges OUT into UTO. LUTON is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London, not in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A large English town in Bedfordshire, known for its airport and football club.

explanation.surface: A fashionable haircut was spotted at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tapered bob is a hairstyle, and small rounded pebbles cover many British beaches.

explanation.surface: Someone is getting a recently married man ready to run for office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for political office?' completes the first sense: one grooms a candidate for office.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare someone for a role is to train them up, and a man on his wedding day is the bridegroom.

clue.text: Disconnect one from Lyon with a jerk

parts.note: un is French for one, and Lyon is a French city
a hitch is a sudden pull or jerk

explanation.surface: A Frenchman suddenly yanks a coupling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a trailer or horse from what it is tied to is to detach it.

clue.text: Some pretty rolling mountainous part of Austria

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the Alps has rather pleasant rolling hills.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alpine region in western Austria famous for its mountains and skiing.

clue.text: He first included college lecturer, one seeking pleasure

indicators.note: included means the lecturer is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
1ST is the abbreviation for first, with the digit read as I
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A man first admitted a university teacher who lives for enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: First is written with the digit 1, read as the letter I; 'included' means the lecturer sits between the other two pieces. 'first' looks like an adverb of order but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives for enjoyment and indulgence pursues pleasure above all.

clue.text: I left capital primarily buying chocolate substitute

indicators.note: left means the letter I has departed from the city name

parts.note: Cairo is the capital of Egypt

indicators.note: primarily means take just the first letter of buying

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a city while shopping for a cocoa alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' drops I from CAIRO leaving CARO, and 'primarily' gives B from buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground pods of the Mediterranean locust bean tree are used as a cocoa replacement.

parts.note: accessory food factor is an old scientific term for a vitamin
B is second in the alphabet, as in plan B
complex means intricate or complicated

explanation.surface: A scientist describes a complicated nutrient that comes second in line.
explanation.walkthrough: Accessory food factor was the early name for vitamins; B, second letter, names the vitamin group.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of water-soluble nutrients including thiamine and riboflavin, collectively a dietary supplement family.
